## Context
Part of #22605: Fix composer keyboard input broken by @FocusState without .focused() binding

## Problem
`ComposerView.swift:73` declares `@FocusState private var composerFocus: Bool` but no view has `.focused($composerFocus)`. After migrating from SwiftUI TextField to ComposerTextEditor (NSViewRepresentable), the `.focused()` modifier was removed but `@FocusState` was kept. SwiftUI's focus reconciliation resets the value, creating a cycle where AppKit focus is established then immediately removed by the reconciliation pass.

## Implementation
- In `clients/macos/vellum-assistant/Features/Chat/ComposerView.swift`:
  - Change line 73 from `@FocusState private var composerFocus: Bool` to `@State private var composerFocus: Bool = false`
  - This is the ONLY change needed — all existing `onChange` handlers and the bidirectional bridge (`composerFocus` ↔ `textViewIsFocused` → `makeFirstResponder`) continue to work correctly with `@State`

## Why this works
- `@State` maintains its value reliably across SwiftUI update cycles (no focus reconciliation interference)
- `onChange(of: composerFocus)` triggers correctly when the value changes
- The existing bridge to `textViewIsFocused` → `ComposerTextEditor.updateNSView` → `makeFirstResponder` handles actual AppKit focus
- All callers that set `composerFocus = true` (`.task`, `.onReceive`, `onChange(of: isInteractionEnabled)`, redirect handler) work identically with `@State`

## Dependencies
- Depends on: none
- Blocks: none

## Overview
Fix cursor misplacement in the composer when typing file paths starting with `/`. The `slashCommandRange` computed property matches `/Users` (and similar) via `^/\w+` regex, triggering the slash highlight overlay even for file paths. This makes the TextField text invisible and renders a `Text` overlay instead — but the two layout engines (NSTextView vs Core Text) compute line wrapping differently, causing the cursor to drift from the visible text on line 2+.

## Goals
- Fix cursor misplacement when pasting/typing file paths in the composer
- Keep slash command highlighting working for actual slash commands

## Non-goals
- Changing the slash command detection/menu behavior (already correct)

## Context
Part of #21778: Fix ToolConfirmationBubble hitbox misalignment on macOS 26

## Implementation

### Fix 1: Wrap onGeometryChange state update in withAnimation(.none)
- **File**: `clients/shared/Features/Chat/ToolConfirmationBubble.swift`
- **Lines 270-271**: Replace `useCompactConfirmationLayout = isCompact` with `withAnimation(.none) { useCompactConfirmationLayout = isCompact }`
- **Why**: Forces synchronous layout invalidation so hit regions are recalculated immediately when the layout mode switches. The bare assignment allows SwiftUI to defer hit-region recalculation on macOS 26.

### Fix 2: Replace if/else layout branch with AnyLayout
- **File**: `clients/shared/Features/Chat/ToolConfirmationBubble.swift`
- **Lines 204-216**: Replace the `if useCompactConfirmationLayout { ... } else { ... }` with a single `AnyLayout` that switches between `VStackLayout` and `HStackLayout`. This preserves child view identity across layout switches, preventing tree destruction and stale hit regions.
- **Requirements**: Must be pixel-identical to current behavior. Compact = actions right-aligned below description. Wide = description and actions side-by-side with Spacer(minLength: VSpacing.md).

### Fix 3: Replace .offset(x: -1) with .padding(.leading, -1)
- **File**: `clients/shared/Features/Chat/ToolConfirmationBubble.swift`
- **Line 239**: Replace `.offset(x: -1)` with `.padding(.leading, -1)` on the "Show details" button HStack.
- **Why**: `.offset()` moves visual position but not the hit region. `.padding()` adjusts both the layout frame and visual position.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: none
- Blocks: none

## Context
Part of #21769: Fix VSplitButton dropdown not responding to clicks

## Implementation

### Fix 1: Color.clear → Color.white.opacity(0.001) in VSplitButton.swift
- **File**: `clients/shared/DesignSystem/Core/Buttons/VSplitButton.swift`
- **Line 84**: Change `Color.clear` to `Color.white.opacity(0.001)`
- **Why**: `Color.clear` can have inconsistent hit-testing with AppKit's NSPopUpButton backing view. A near-zero-opacity color is visually invisible but reliably registers as a tappable area.

### Fix 2: Add .allowsHitTesting(false) to overlay in ToolConfirmationBubble.swift
- **File**: `clients/shared/Features/Chat/ToolConfirmationBubble.swift`
- **Lines 464-467**: Add `.allowsHitTesting(false)` to the `.overlay(RoundedRectangle(...).strokeBorder(...))` on the allowSplitButton
- **Why**: The keyboard selection overlay covers the entire VSplitButton and can intercept taps before they reach the Menu inside the ZStack.

### Fix 3: Remove .clipped() from dropdown ZStack in VSplitButton.swift
- **File**: `clients/shared/DesignSystem/Core/Buttons/VSplitButton.swift`
- **Line 93**: Remove `.clipped()` from the dropdown zone ZStack
- **Why**: `.clipped()` can interfere with Menu's internal AppKit hosting hit region. The parent `clipShape` already handles visual bounds.

## Context
Part of #21550: Restore server-side message pagination on HTTP endpoint

## Implementation

### 3a. Remove trim-after-pagination (prevents infinite fetch-trim loop)
- File: `clients/shared/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift` (line 3069)
- Remove the `trimOldMessagesIfNeeded()` call in the `isPaginationLoad` branch of `populateFromHistory()`
- Add a `// TODO:` comment noting pagination-aware trim as follow-up
- Why: After prepending pages, total can exceed trimThreshold (150), triggering trim which removes just-fetched messages and resets cursor -> infinite loop. The pagination branch was never exercised before (daemon never returned hasMore=true), so removing this call cannot regress existing behavior.

### 3b. Add safety timeout using resetMessagePagination()
- File: `clients/shared/Features/Chat/ChatViewModel.swift` (lines 889-893)
- Extend the existing 30s timeout task with a second stage at 60s that calls `resetMessagePagination()`:
  ```swift
  loadMoreTimeoutTask = Task { @MainActor [weak self] in
      try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 30_000_000_000) // 30s
      guard let self, !Task.isCancelled, self.isLoadingMoreMessages else { return }
      log.warning("Pagination request still pending after 30s — daemon may be unresponsive")
      try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 30_000_000_000) // +30s = 60s total
      guard let self, !Task.isCancelled, self.isLoadingMoreMessages else { return }
      log.error("Pagination request timed out after 60s — resetting pagination state")
      self.resetMessagePagination()
  }
  ```
- Why: `resetMessagePagination()` is safer than hard-clearing `isLoadingMoreMessages` because it resets ALL pagination state. Late responses are safely dropped at `pendingHistoryByConversationId` lookup.

- Blocks: none

## Overview
Scrolling up in a conversation fails to load messages before ~March 21st. The daemon's `GET /v1/messages` HTTP endpoint ignores all pagination parameters and always returns every message. Pagination was previously implemented on the WebSocket IPC transport (#9227, #9246) but was deleted as "dead code" (#16207) when the client migrated to HTTP, without porting the logic to the HTTP handler.

## Goals
- Restore server-side pagination in `handleListMessages` (Option A: only paginate when `beforeTimestamp` is present)
- Add composite DB index for efficient paginated queries
- Fix client-side trim-after-pagination infinite loop
- Add safety timeout for stuck pagination loading state

## Non-goals
- `mode` / `maxTextChars` / `maxToolResultChars` content truncation
- `beforeMessageId` tie-breaker cursor on client side
- Client-side dedup on pagination prepend
- Pagination-aware memory trim (follow-up)
- N+1 attachment query optimization

## Approach
Option A: Only paginate when `beforeTimestamp` is present in the query. Initial load and reconnect requests (which send `limit` but no `beforeTimestamp`) continue returning all messages — zero regression risk. The "load more" scroll-up path (which sends both `limit` and `beforeTimestamp`) gets proper pagination support.

## Feature branch
`feature/msg-pagination`

## Milestones
- [ ] M1: Add composite DB index and `getMessagesPaginated()` to conversation-crud
- [ ] M2: Wire pagination into `handleListMessages` HTTP endpoint
- [ ] M3: Client-side safety fixes (trim loop + stuck loading timeout)
- [ ] M4: Add pagination test suite

payload.author: Jasonnnz
payload.body:
## Overview
When the user presses the stop button while the assistant is executing a task, the stop signal does not actually terminate work running on the macOS client (host bash, host file, and host CU proxies). The daemon resolves its pending promise with "Aborted" but never sends a cancel message to the Swift client, leaving processes running. Additionally, MCP tool calls are completely uncancellable, and grandchild processes can survive SIGKILL on macOS.

## Goals
- Host-proxied tool execution (bash, file, CU) is actually killed when stop is pressed
- Stale result POSTs from cancelled operations are suppressed on the Swift side
- MCP tool calls respect the AbortSignal for cooperative cancellation
- Child process groups are properly cleaned up on macOS

## Non-goals
- Redesigning the ctx.processing state machine for edge-case race windows
- Adding AbortSignal to Playwright direct calls (covered via MCP cancellation)
- Enforcing cancellation in host-mode skill scripts (cooperative only)

## Approach
Three-layer fix:
1. **Wire protocol**: Add cancel message types for all three host proxies (bash, file, CU)
2. **Daemon**: Send cancel messages when AbortSignal fires in proxy onAbort handlers
3. **Swift client**: Handle cancel messages — kill processes, cancel tasks, dismiss overlays, suppress stale POSTs with TTL-based tracking
4. **MCP**: Thread AbortSignal through the MCP call chain using the SDK's native signal support
5. **Process groups**: Use detached spawn + process group kill for reliable grandchild cleanup

## Feature branch

## Context
Part of #21195: Hatch progress bar for setup flow

## Implementation

### `clients/macos/vellum-assistant/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingFlowView.swift`

#### 1. Managed path progress in `awaitManagedAssistantReady()`

Set progress at three phase boundaries (after `isHatching = true`, so HatchingStepView is rendering):

| Point in code | step | label | target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before awaitAssistantProvisioned (~line 356) | 1/3 | "Provisioning assistant..." | 0.33 |
| Before health poll loop (~line 369) | 2/3 | "Connecting to assistant..." | 0.66 |
| On response.isSuccess (~line 376) | 3/3 | "Ready" | 1.0 |

Add completion guard: `guard !state.hatchCompleted else { return }` before each update.

Note: No step 0 in `performManagedBootstrap()` — that phase shows `managedBootstrapView` with its own spinner, not HatchingStepView. Managed sets `hatchCompleted` immediately on health success (no pre-delay).

#### 2. Centralized post-complete presentation delay

Replace existing `onChange(of: state.hatchCompleted)` (line 237-239) with:

```swift
@State private var didCallComplete = false
@State private var completionDelayTask: Task<Void, Never>?

.onChange(of: state.hatchCompleted) { _, completed in
    if completed {
        guard !didCallComplete else { return }
        didCallComplete = true
        completionDelayTask = Task {
            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 1_000_000_000)
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            onComplete()
        }
    }
}
.onDisappear { completionDelayTask?.cancel() }
```

This prevents duplicate `onComplete()` calls and gives the user 1.0s to see bar → 100% + "Your assistant is ready!" before the view closes.

#### Timing Summary
| Path | Pre-hatchCompleted | Post-hatchCompleted | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLI (local/docker/gcp/aws) | 0.5s (handleHatchSuccess, from M4) | 1.0s (this change) | ~1.5s |
| Managed | 0s (immediate) | 1.0s (this change) | ~1.0s |

## Dependencies
- Depends on: M3 (progress properties)
- Blocks: none

## Context
Part of #21195: Hatch progress bar for setup flow

## Implementation

### `clients/macos/vellum-assistant/Features/Onboarding/HatchingStepView.swift`

#### 1. Parse HATCH_PROGRESS events in `startRemoteHatch()` onOutput callback

In the `onOutput` closure, before appending to `state.hatchLogLines`:
- Check `line.hasPrefix("HATCH_PROGRESS:")`
- Guard: `!state.hatchCompleted && completionTask == nil` (ignore late events after success starts)
- Parse JSON payload: `{"step":N,"total":M,"label":"..."}`
- Validate bounds: `total > 0 && step >= 0 && step <= total`
- Update: `state.hatchCurrentStep`, `state.hatchTotalSteps`, `state.hatchStepLabel`, `state.hatchProgressTarget = Double(step) / Double(total)`
- Return early — don't append sentinel lines to `hatchLogLines`

#### 2. Computed property for visibility

```swift
var showProgressBar: Bool {
    !state.hatchFailed && !state.hatchCompleted && !isCustomHardware && state.hatchStepLabel != nil
}
```

#### 3. Progress section view (Layout Option A)

Add between `statusText` and `failureButtons` in the body:

```swift
if showProgressBar {
    VStack(spacing: VSpacing.xs) {
        ProgressView(value: state.hatchProgressDisplay)
            .frame(maxWidth: 240)
        if let label = state.hatchStepLabel {
            Text(label)
                .font(.system(size: 12))
                .foregroundColor(VColor.contentTertiary)
        }
    }
    .transition(.opacity.animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.3)))
}
```

Layout:
```
    [  avatar  ]
     Waking up...
  Hang tight — your assistant...
    [████████░░░░░░░░]
   Pulling Docker images...
```

#### 4. Smooth interpolation (creep timer)

`TimelineView(.animation)` that runs while hatching active and `hatchStepLabel != nil`:
- Compute `ceiling = min((currentStep + 1) / totalSteps - 0.02, 0.95)`
- If `displayProgress < targetProgress`: lerp with factor 0.15 (~200ms catchup)
- If `displayProgress >= targetProgress` but `< ceiling`: creep at 0.0003/frame (~1%/s)
- Clamp to `ceiling`
- On `hatchCompleted`: target → 1.0, lerp animates there
- On `hatchFailed`: stop timer, freeze bar

#### 5. Reduce handleHatchSuccess delay

Change from 1.5s to 0.5s (line 234). Combined with 1.0s post-complete delay in OnboardingFlowView (M5) = ~1.5s total for CLI paths.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: M1 (CLI events), M2 (line buffering), M3 (progress properties)
- Blocks: none

## Context
Part of #21195: Hatch progress bar for setup flow

## Implementation

### `clients/macos/vellum-assistant/App/VellumCli.swift` — `runRemoteHatch()` method

The `readabilityHandler` on `Pipe` delivers arbitrary `Data` chunks, not guaranteed line-delimited strings. The current code trims whitespace and passes the result to `onOutput`, which loses newline boundaries. This means `HATCH_PROGRESS:` sentinel lines can be split across chunks or merged with other lines.

**Changes:**
1. Add two separate `Data` line buffers (one for stdout, one for stderr) as local variables before the pipe handlers
2. In each `readabilityHandler`:
   - Append incoming `Data` to the buffer
   - Split buffer on `\n` (0x0A byte)
   - Emit all complete lines via `onOutput` (stdout) or `stderrAccumulator` (stderr)
   - Keep the last incomplete fragment as the new buffer
3. In the `terminationHandler`, flush any remaining data in both buffers as final lines
4. stderr continues feeding `StderrAccumulator` for `CLI_ERROR:`/`DAEMON_ERROR:` parsing — unchanged behavior
5. Only stdout lines participate in `HATCH_PROGRESS:` parsing (done in M4)

**Key constraint:** Must NOT break existing behavior:
- `onOutput` still receives trimmed, complete lines
- `stderrAccumulator` still accumulates all stderr for error parsing
- Docker readiness sentinel detection still works
- Existing log output to `os.Logger` unchanged

## Dependencies
- Depends on: none
- Blocks: M4 (parsing assumes line-buffered output)

## Context
Part of #21186: Add retry logic to conversation list fetch on app restart

## Problem
When `connect()` fails in `GatewayConnectionManager`, there is no retry mechanism. The health check loop only starts after a successful connection, and `autoWakeIfAssistantDied()` only fires when an established connection drops. After a quit/restart race where the initial connection fails, the app stays permanently disconnected.

## Implementation
- Add `reconnectionTask: Task<Void, Never>?` property to `GatewayConnectionManager`
- Add `startReconnectionLoop()` method (macOS only, local assistants only)
  - Increasing delays: 3s, 5s, 10s, then 15s cap
  - Each attempt: performHealthCheck(), if fails try auto-wake
  - On success: start health check loop + SSE, stop loop
  - Checks Task.isCancelled and isConnected before each attempt
- Call `startReconnectionLoop()` from `connectImpl()`'s catch block
- Cancel `reconnectionTask` in `disconnect()` and `reconfigure()`
- Do NOT cancel in `disconnectInternal()` (called by connectImpl during retries)

- Depends on: M1 (#21187)
- Blocks: none

## Overview
Replace hand-rolled LRU caches with NSCache and fix main-thread blocking during scroll in old conversations. The current caches use O(n) min(by:) eviction which compounds during cold-scroll bursts when LazyVStack materializes many cells simultaneously.

## Goals
- Eliminate O(n) LRU eviction scans during cache insertion bursts
- Move synchronous file I/O off the main thread in AnimatedImageView
- Cache expensive ChatBubble.init() computations for completed messages
- Reduce rainbow spinner occurrences when scrolling up in long conversations

## Non-goals
- Changing markdown parsing logic or segment types
- Modifying LazyVStack pagination behavior
- Adding new UI features

## Approach
Four independent milestones, each targeting a specific source of main-thread blocking:
1. Replace segmentCache with NSCache (eliminates O(n) eviction + manual byte tracking)
2. Replace attributedStringCache with NSCache + cache prefix widths (eliminates repeated Core Text layout)
3. Move AnimatedImageView file I/O to Task.detached + cache workspace dir
4. Memoize ChatBubble interleaved content computation by message identity

## Feature branch
`feature/nscache-scroll-perf`

## Milestones
- [ ] M1: Replace segmentCache with NSCache in ChatBubbleTextContent
- [ ] M2: Replace attributedStringCache with NSCache + cache prefix widths in MarkdownSegmentView
- [ ] M3: Move AnimatedImageView file I/O off main thread
- [ ] M4: Memoize ChatBubble interleaved content computation

payload.body:
## Problem

When sending a message, the conversation tail avatar briefly disappears and then reappears when the assistant response starts streaming. This is most noticeable when:
- The "thinking" indicator appears
- A rich UI element (tool confirmation, surface widget) expands

## Root cause

When the LazyVStack re-layouts during content changes (new message added, thinking indicator inserted, rich UI expanding), the `ConversationTailAnchorYKey` preference temporarily reports `.infinity` because the anchor view gets deallocated and recreated by the LazyVStack. 

In `updateAvatarFollower()` (`MessageListView.swift:462-468`), a non-finite anchor Y immediately sets `avatarDisplayY = .infinity`, which hides the avatar overlay. Once the layout settles and the anchor reports a finite value again, the avatar reappears — but there's a visible flash.

## Proposed fix

When `isSending` is true and `avatarDisplayY` is already finite, skip the `.infinity` reset on transient non-finite anchor values. The avatar stays at its last known position during the brief layout transition. When the anchor comes back with a real value, the avatar smoothly updates to the new position.

```swift
guard anchorY.isFinite else {
    avatarSmoothingTask?.cancel()
    avatarSmoothingTask = nil
    scrollTracking.pendingAvatarY = nil
    scrollTracking.avatarLastAppliedAt = nil
    // Don't hide the avatar during active send — the non-finite anchor
    // is transient (LazyVStack deallocating/recreating the anchor view).
    // Keep the avatar at its last known position until a finite anchor returns.
    if !isSending, avatarDisplayY != .infinity {
        avatarDisplayY = .infinity
    }
    return
}
```

## Context

Identified during work on #20942 (fix main thread stall during message send). The avatar disappearance is pre-existing behavior, not introduced by #20942.

## Log evidence

```
16:31:18.449  BottomPin detach
16:31:18.465  Anchor preference non-finite — marking anchor invisible (deallocated by LazyVStack)
16:31:18.617  Non-finite scroll geometry detected
16:31:19.096  BottomPin reattach
```

~600ms gap where the avatar is hidden during an active send.
payload.title: fix: avatar disappears briefly when thinking indicator or rich UI appears after send

## Overview
Fix the spinning beach ball caused by scroll loop feedback cycles in normal chat conversations. The circuit breaker (ChatScrollLoopGuard) detects the loop but fails to suppress the avatar follower feedback path, allowing body re-evaluations to continue unchecked. Additionally, duplicate scroll detectors compete over scroll state without automatic resolution.

## Goals
- Break the avatar follower feedback loop when the scroll loop guard trips
- Prevent duplicate scroll detectors from fighting over scroll state
- Eliminate beach ball on normal conversations without affecting scroll behavior when healthy

- Modifying the bottom pin coordinator retry logic

## Approach
Two targeted fixes that extend existing safety mechanisms to cover gaps:
1. Check `scrollLoopGuard.isTripped()` in `updateAvatarFollower()` and `applyAvatarDisplayY()` to suppress @State mutations during detected loops
2. Skip scroll event callbacks in ScrollWheelDetector when duplicate detectors are detected for the same conversation/window pair

## Context
Part of the precomputedState memoization epic.

## Problem
`precomputedState` is a computed property (line 250 of MessageListView.swift) that runs O(N) scans on every body evaluation. Body re-evaluates on every scroll tick (via snapshotDebounceTask @State, avatarDisplayY @State, etc.), but the inputs to precomputedState (messages, isSending, isThinking, isCompacting, activeSubagents, assistantStatusText, displayedMessageCount) don't change during scroll.

## Implementation

1. Create a cache key struct that captures all inputs:
```swift
private struct PrecomputedInputs: Equatable {
    let messageIds: [UUID]
    let messageLastModified: [Date]  // or use message equality
    let isSending: Bool
    let isThinking: Bool
    let isCompacting: Bool
    let assistantStatusText: String?
    let activeSubagentIds: Set<String>
    let displayedMessageCount: Int
}
```

Note: For messages, we need to detect content changes too (streaming tokens update message text). Using `messages.map { $0.id }` alone won't catch streaming updates. Consider using `messages.map { "\($0.id)-\($0.text.count)-\($0.toolCalls.count)-\($0.isStreaming)" }` or make ChatMessage conform to Equatable if it doesn't already, and compare `messages` directly.

2. Add @State storage for the cache on the `MessageListView` struct (not on ScrollTrackingState — this needs to persist across body evaluations but also needs to trigger re-render when it changes... actually, store on ScrollTrackingState since we DON'T want cache changes to trigger re-render):

```swift
// On ScrollTrackingState class (non-reactive):
var cachedPrecomputedInputs: PrecomputedInputs?
var cachedPrecomputedState: PrecomputedMessageListState?
```

3. Update `precomputedState` to check the cache:
```swift
private var precomputedState: PrecomputedMessageListState {
    let currentInputs = PrecomputedInputs(...)
    if let cached = scrollTracking.cachedPrecomputedInputs,
       cached == currentInputs,
       let cachedState = scrollTracking.cachedPrecomputedState {
        return cachedState
    }
    // ... existing computation ...
    let result = PrecomputedMessageListState(...)
    scrollTracking.cachedPrecomputedInputs = currentInputs
    scrollTracking.cachedPrecomputedState = result
    return result
}
```

4. Add DEBUG validation:
```swift
#if DEBUG
// Validate cache correctness by comparing against fresh computation
if let cached = scrollTracking.cachedPrecomputedState,
   scrollTracking.cachedPrecomputedInputs == currentInputs {
    let fresh = computePrecomputedState() // extract computation to a function
    assert(cached.displayMessages.count == fresh.displayMessages.count, "precomputedState cache stale: displayMessages count mismatch")
}
#endif
```

## Key risk
Missing an input dependency means stale UI. The inputs must capture EVERYTHING that affects the output. Check every variable read inside `precomputedState` that comes from the view's properties (not from local computation).

## Files
- `clients/macos/vellum-assistant/Features/Chat/MessageListView.swift`
payload.title: M1: Memoize precomputedState behind input equality check

## Overview
Memoize `precomputedState` in `MessageListView` so the O(N) computation (timestamp grouping, confirmation scanning, turn detection, subagent grouping) only runs when its inputs actually change — not on every scroll-triggered body re-evaluation.

## Goals
- Skip O(N) precomputedState recomputation when only scroll-related @State changed (avatarDisplayY, hasFreshAnchorMeasurement, etc.)
- Retain correctness: recompute when messages, isSending, isThinking, isCompacting, activeSubagents, or assistantStatusText change

- Changing the scroll architecture or preference key system
- Reducing body re-evaluation frequency (addressed separately)

Store the last-computed inputs and output in @State. On each body evaluation, compare current inputs against cached inputs. If unchanged, return cached output. If changed, recompute and cache. Add a DEBUG assertion that validates the cache by comparing against a fresh computation.

`feature/memoize-precomputed-state`

## Context
Part of #20921: scroll performance batch 1

## Problem
`ChatBubble.formattedTimestamp` (line 213), `ChatBubble.detailedTimestamp` (line 232), and `TimestampDivider.formattedTime` (line 56) each allocate new `DateFormatter` instances on every body evaluation. `DateFormatter` init is one of the most expensive ObjC bridge operations. With 50 visible bubbles, that's 100+ allocations per render pass.

## Implementation
Add static formatters. Note: timezone must still be resolved per-call since `ChatTimestampTimeZone.resolve()` can change. The optimization is avoiding the `DateFormatter()` allocation — the timezone assignment on a static instance is cheap.

In `ChatBubble.swift`, add static formatters and update the computed properties to use them:
```swift
private static let timeFormatter: DateFormatter = {
    let f = DateFormatter()
    f.dateStyle = .none
    f.timeStyle = .short
    return f
}()
private static let dayFormatter: DateFormatter = {
    let f = DateFormatter()
    f.dateFormat = "MMM d"
    return f
}()
private static let detailedFormatter: DateFormatter = {
    let f = DateFormatter()
    f.dateStyle = .full
    f.timeStyle = .long
    return f
}()
```
Then update `formattedTimestamp`, `detailedTimestamp` to set `.timeZone` on the static formatters before use.

Same pattern in `TimestampDivider.swift` for its `formattedTime`.

- `clients/macos/vellum-assistant/Features/Chat/ChatBubble.swift`

payload.author: Jasonnnz
payload.body:
## Overview
Fix the primary cause of rainbow spinners during scroll-up: `NSSharingService.sharingServicesForItems()` is called synchronously on the main thread inside SwiftUI view bodies for every image in the conversation, on every render pass. CPU profiling shows this accounts for 98.2% of main thread blocking during scroll — each call triggers synchronous XPC roundtrips to PlugInKit to discover sharing extensions.

## Goals
- Eliminate synchronous XPC calls from the SwiftUI render path
- Cache sharing service discovery per file extension (services depend on type, not content)
- Move temp file writes from render time to user action time

## Non-goals
- Changing the sharing UI or available services
- Removing NSSharingService support

## Approach

## Context
Part of #20387: fix guardian token race condition on first launch

## Problem
In `AppDelegate+DaemonSetup.swift`, `setupDaemonClient()` spawns a Task that calls `connect()` at line 265. `connect()` does a health check via `GatewayHTTPClient` which reads `ActorTokenManager.getToken()` from the Keychain. On first launch, the Keychain is empty because `ensureActorCredentials()` (which imports the guardian token) runs later in `proceedToApp()` as a separate concurrent Task. The health check gets 401, and `connect()` fails.

## Implementation
In `setupDaemonClient()`'s Task body, right before the `connect()` call (line 262), add:

```swift
if let assistantId = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: "connectedAssistantId"),
   !ActorTokenManager.hasToken {
    _ = GuardianTokenFileReader.importIfAvailable(assistantId: assistantId)
}
```

## Files to modify
- `clients/macos/vellum-assistant/App/AppDelegate+DaemonSetup.swift`

## Dependencies
- Depends on: none
- Blocks: none

## Overview
Fix a race condition introduced in #20372 where `setupDaemonClient()` calls `connect()` before `ensureActorCredentials()` has imported the guardian token into the Keychain. On first launch, the health check fires with no auth header, gets 401, and fails with `ConnectionError.healthCheckFailed`.

## Goals
- Ensure the guardian token is in the Keychain before `connect()` fires the health check
- Fix first-launch daemon connection failures

## Non-goals
- Restructuring the `proceedToApp()` task ordering
- Changing `ensureActorCredentials()` or its refresh loop

## Approach
Add a synchronous `GuardianTokenFileReader.importIfAvailable()` call inside `setupDaemonClient()`'s Task, right before `connect()`, guarded by `!ActorTokenManager.hasToken`. This is the same import call already used in `performInitialBootstrap()` — we're just running it earlier so the token is available when `connect()` needs it.

## Feature branch
`feature/fix-guardian-token-race`

## Context
Part of #20376: Fix scroll-up rainbow spinner by moving snapshotDebounceTask off @State

## Problem
`snapshotDebounceTask` is declared as `@State private var snapshotDebounceTask: Task<Void, Never>?` on `MessageListView` (line 216). Every time `scheduleTranscriptSnapshot()` is called (on every scroll tick that passes the 2pt dead-zone via `AnchorMinYKey.onPreferenceChange`), the `@State` is reassigned, triggering a full `MessageListView.body` re-evaluation. This causes the O(N) `precomputedState` to recompute and all `MessageCellView.==` checks to run — for no visual change.

## Implementation
1. Add a `snapshotDebounceTask: Task<Void, Never>?` property to the `ScrollTrackingState` class (line ~63 in MessageListView.swift). This class is explicitly designed for non-reactive scroll tracking state per the comment at lines 218-219.
2. Remove the `@State private var snapshotDebounceTask` declaration (line 216) and its doc comment (lines 214-215).
3. Update `scheduleTranscriptSnapshot()` (lines 730-737) to reference `scrollTracking.snapshotDebounceTask` instead of `snapshotDebounceTask`.

## Files to modify
- `clients/macos/vellum-assistant/Features/Chat/MessageListView.swift`

## Dependencies
- Depends on: none
- Blocks: none
payload.title: M1: Move snapshotDebounceTask from @State to ScrollTrackingState

payload.author: Jasonnnz
payload.body:
## Overview
Fix rainbow spinner (beach ball) lag when scrolling up in the chat by moving `snapshotDebounceTask` from `@State` to the non-reactive `ScrollTrackingState` class. Currently, `scheduleTranscriptSnapshot()` reassigns a `@State Task` on every scroll tick that passes the 2pt dead-zone, triggering unnecessary `MessageListView.body` re-evaluations with O(N) `precomputedState` scans — even though nothing about the messages has changed.

## Goals
- Eliminate the dominant source of per-frame body re-evaluations during scroll-up
- Reduce main-thread work during scroll to prevent rainbow spinners on long conversations

## Non-goals
- Changing the scroll architecture or preference key system
- Optimizing `precomputedState` computation itself (future work)
- Addressing `avatarDisplayY`-driven re-evaluations (visually necessary, separate concern)

## Approach
Move `snapshotDebounceTask` from `@State private var` on `MessageListView` to a stored property on `ScrollTrackingState` (the non-reactive class at line 220, explicitly designed for "non-reactive scroll tracking state"). This breaks the chain: `AnchorMinYKey fires → scheduleTranscriptSnapshot() → @State mutation → body re-eval → O(N) precomputedState`. The task still runs, still debounces, but the assignment no longer triggers SwiftUI body re-evaluation.

## Feature branch
`feature/scroll-perf-snapshot-task`

## Milestones
- [ ] M1: Move snapshotDebounceTask from @State to ScrollTrackingState

## Context
Part of #19747: Fix scroll-to-bottom button not appearing consistently

## Problem
In `MessageListView.swift`, `configureBottomPinCoordinator(proxy:)` is called in `onAppear`, but the `ScrollWheelDetector`'s NSEvent monitor is installed in `makeNSView` (which runs earlier). If a scroll-up event fires during the brief window between `makeNSView` and `onAppear`, `detach()` is called on the coordinator with `onFollowStateChanged` still `nil`. This means `isNearBottom` is never set to `false`. Worse, subsequent scroll-up events see `wasFollowing = false` and skip the callback entirely, leaving `isNearBottom` permanently stuck at `true`.

## Implementation
- In `configureBottomPinCoordinator(proxy:)` (~line 805 of MessageListView.swift):
  - After setting `bottomPinCoordinator.onFollowStateChanged`, check if the coordinator is already in detached state (`!bottomPinCoordinator.isFollowingBottom`)
  - If so, immediately sync `isNearBottom = false` to catch up with the coordinator's state

## Dependencies
- Depends on: none
- Blocks: none

## Context
Part of #19747: Fix scroll-to-bottom button not appearing consistently

## Problem
In `MessageListView.swift`, the `.onPreferenceChange(AnchorMinYKey.self)` handler uses `PreferenceGeometryFilter.evaluate()` which rejects non-finite values (`.infinity`). When the LazyVStack deallocates the `scroll-bottom-anchor` (because the user scrolled far from the bottom), the preference fires with `.infinity` (the PreferenceKey default). This value is silently discarded, leaving `anchorTracker.isVisible` stuck at `true` and `anchorTracker.lastMinY` frozen at the last finite measurement. Since the button requires `!anchorTracker.isVisible`, it never shows.

## Implementation
- In the `.onPreferenceChange(AnchorMinYKey.self)` handler (~line 1138 of MessageListView.swift):
  - When `PreferenceGeometryFilter.evaluate()` returns `.rejectNonFinite`, explicitly set `anchorTracker.isVisible = false` instead of returning early
  - Keep `anchorTracker.lastMinY` unchanged (no real measurement to update with)
  - The `.rejectDeadZone` case should continue to return early as before
  - Add a log statement for diagnostics

## Dependencies
- Depends on: none
- Blocks: none

payload.body:
## Overview
Fix the "Scroll to latest" button not appearing consistently when scrolling up in conversations (both forked and regular). The root cause is twofold: (1) the macOS `PreferenceGeometryFilter` silently rejects `.infinity` values from `AnchorMinYKey` when the LazyVStack deallocates the scroll anchor, leaving `anchorTracker.isVisible` stuck at `true`, and (2) a race condition where the `bottomPinCoordinator.onFollowStateChanged` callback is nil during the brief window between `makeNSView` and `onAppear`.

## Goals
- Fix the primary failure mode: anchor deallocation leaving `isVisible` stuck at `true`
- Fix the secondary race condition: coordinator callback not set during view remount
- Ensure the scroll-to-bottom button appears reliably across all conversation types

## Non-goals
- iOS scroll changes (iOS handles `.infinity` correctly already)
- Refactoring the preference filter system
- Changing the dead-zone threshold

## Approach
Two targeted fixes in `MessageListView.swift`:
1. Handle the `.rejectNonFinite` case in the `AnchorMinYKey` preference handler by setting `anchorTracker.isVisible = false` when the anchor is deallocated
2. Sync coordinator follow state after callback setup in `configureBottomPinCoordinator`

## Feature branch
`feature/fix-scroll-to-bottom-btn`

## Milestones
- [ ] M1: Handle non-finite AnchorMinYKey preference values
- [ ] M2: Sync coordinator follow state after callback setup
